messages:
maria_support: FYI - Acme (APAC) filed an urgent ticket: p99 jumped after last night's quant profile swap to int8 for model:v2. Customer reports latency from ~380ms -> ~1.2s p99, p95 from ~120ms -> ~450ms. Ticket #INC-2026. They say it started at ~02:15 UTC when the profile rollout finished.

acme-eng: Confirming. We saw a huge tail on inference after the new profile. Happens on both small and large inputs, more visible under sustained QPS.

leo_sre: Can you paste a repro request + headers (X-Request-ID) and the region/route? Also which quantization profile name was applied?

maria_support: Customer sent sample curl: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-like-v2","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":128}'
```
They included trace header X-Request-ID: acme-req-7052. Profile: "quant_profile:int8-mixed-calib-v3" deployed to apac-1.

anya_ml: Initial hypothesis: this profile introduced an int8 path which increases per-token variance for certain sequence lengths and triggers extra kernel fallbacks or dequantization steps on GPU. Need perf logs from runtime: compile queue, kernel fallback counts, and kvcache hit rates.

maria_support: Attached runtime logs from customer timeframe (excerpt):
```
[02:15:23] compile_queue: enqueue model redwood/gpt-like-v2 quant:int8-mixed-calib-v3
[02:15:24] kernel_selector: using int8-kernel v7, fallback_count=0
[02:16:01] batch_executor: batch_size=1 delayed=12ms due_to_kvcache_miss
[02:16:04] kv_cache: miss_rate spike 0.72 -> 0.95
[02:16:04] latency: p99 1200ms p95 450ms
[02:16:05] kernel_selector: runtime fallback to fp16-kernel for some ops (reason: unstable accumulation)
```

leo_sre: Kernel fallback observed — that explains the large jumps. Fallbacks are expensive and cause CPU/GPU synchronization spikes. Do we know which ops triggered fallback? Any NaN/overflow logs?

anya_ml: The int8 calibration might underflow/overflow in attention accumulation for long sequences; when accumulation exceeds int8 dynamic range we trigger a fallback to fp16 for safety (we've seen that before). That fallback often happens mid-sequence which kills batching and raises p99.

dan_runtime: Mitigations I can push immediately: (1) runtime route for acme -> force model variant redwood/gpt-like-v2:fp16 for apac-1; (2) enable "quant_fallback_strategy: per-request-atomic" to fail fast and use fp16 for that request instead of partial fallback; (3) temporarily lower max_batch_delay to reduce wide batching variance. Which one do we want now?

maria_support: Customer asked for fastest fix. Recommend (1) route them to fp16 variant and (2) roll the int8 profile back for apac-1. Can we do both?

dan_runtime: I applied a routing override for tenant acme -> model_variant=fp16 at 02:18 UTC. ops-bot: applied route-change acme apac-1 -> fp16 (change_id: ch-3412345700).

ops-bot: route-change applied: ch-3412345700 by dan_runtime at 02:18:10 UTC.

acme-eng: Seeing immediate improvement in tail. p99 down to ~420ms within 2 mins. Thanks.

leo_sre: Good. Next steps: gather full perf traces for correlation. Collect the following for the incident window: 
- runtime kernel_selector logs (all reasons for fallback)
- GPU utilization / SM stalls
- batch sizes and max_batch_delay distribution
- kvcache hit/miss traces per request-id
- any cuda error / NaN reports

maria_support: I'll request those from the customer and attach ticket. Also asking them to run a short synthetic test we can deploy: 10k requests over 10m with X-Request-ID prefix to correlate.

anya_ml: Longer-term: "int8-mixed-calib-v3" needs re-calibration for APAC traffic pattern. Actions:
- run calibration harness with APAC prompt distribution (prefix lengths, token histograms)
- increase clipping thresholds for attention accumulators or use symmetric per-channel scaling
- consider fp8 shadow runs to see quality vs perf tradeoff (if hardware supports)

dan_runtime: For rollout policy changes: we should never do global profile swaps without per-region canary + 1h watch. Propose restore: profile->int8 on 5% traffic for 30m with auto-rollback on p99 increase >20%. Add a runtime flag "force_fp16_on_kernel_fallback" so fallback is not partial.

leo_sre: Also investigate KV cache interaction: high miss_rate suggests cache warmup causing small batches which increase per-token overhead. If we prewarm kvcache for high-QPS tenants or pin hot prefixes, that might reduce misses.

maria_support: Customer accepted routing change and asks for timeline on root cause and whether we will prevent recurrence. I've told them we'll follow up with a calibration patch + safer rollout plan.

anya_ml: I'll own calibration. ETA initial findings 48h. Plan: run calib sweep on representative APAC corpus, produce new quant_profile:int8-mixed-calib-v3.1 with adjusted thresholds.

dan_runtime: I'll update rollout docs and add an automated rollback threshold. I'll also add an emergency runtime control to force fp16 for a tenant.

leo_sre: I'll stitch traces once we have X-Request-IDs and confirm which ops triggered fallback.

maria_support: Summary for ticket INC-2026: 1) Immediate: routed ACME to fp16 variant (ch-3412345700) -> p99 improved. 2) Short: collect traces, run synthetic load, gather kernel fallback data. 3) Medium: re-calibrate int8 profile for APAC, add safer canary rollout. 4) Long: add per-tenant runtime guardrails (force_fp16_on_fallback, per-region canary). Owners: maria_support (customer comms), anya_ml (calibration), dan_runtime (routing + rollout safeguards), leo_sre (post-incident trace).

acme-eng: Thanks team. Please keep us posted, we need a follow-up patch before next scheduled maintenance. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Will update INC-2026 with owners and next check-in in 4h.

leo_sre: Filing a follow-up internal ticket: SRE-4781 quant-fallback-triage referencing INC-2026.

ops-bot: ticket SRE-4781 created by leo_sre at 02:36 UTC.

maria_support: Closing thread here, moving active follow-ups into the ticket. If anyone finds additional correlated errors (OOM, NaN) drop them into the ticket.
